transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-02-03
Start: 10:30 AM PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Ravi Kumar (NexaHealth), Elena Torres (NexaHealth), Samir Patel (NexaHealth), Priya Rao (NexaHealth)

Summary: quick onboarding progress check, environment access checklist, security questions, plan for on-prem benchmark, follow-ups on dedicated vs hosted sizing. Some ASR glitches on product names (Redwood Private flagged as "Redwood privatee" in transcript).

Topics:
- Access & networking (VPC peering, IAM, k8s staging access)
- Security/compliance follow-ups (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
- Benchmark plan and datasets for latency/throughput tuning
- Pilot next steps and success criteria

Transcript:
00:00 Maya: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is our weekly POC sync for Nexa, um Devon and I plus Jordan are here from Redwood, and uh Ravi, Elena, Samir, Priya thanks for the time.
00:08 Ravi: yep thanks Maya, good morning. quick agenda check, we wanted to confirm staging access and the benchmark plan.
00:14 Maya: yep that is the plan, we'll go through checklist, and then Devon will run through the perf plan.
00:21 Elena: just to note we had a hiccup last night with our bastion host, so k8s access is not fully ready, Samir is on it.
00:29 Samir: yeah sorry about that, our infra team changed a rule, will revert and share the details shortly.
00:35 Devon: cool, on my side I prepared a small suite of 2,000 queries representative of the production mix, mostly short prompts, some chat style. intend to run with 1) hosted Redwood endpoint, 2) dedicated pilot on our small gpu pool, and 3) on-prem stager.
00:55 Priya: quick question, is the prod mix including embeddings? we have both gen and embed workloads.
01:02 Devon: yes, we'll separate the tests, embeddings run at different throughput. for generation we care about 95th latency and tokens per second.
01:12 Ravi: our primary success metric is 95th < 250ms for single-turn queries and steady 50 qps sustained for batching use case. if we can't hit that we need fallback plan.
01:23 Maya: noted. on the security side Jordan, I'll hand it over to you for the compliance items.
01:28 Jordan: sure, Nexa asked for SOC2 report and an ISO addendum, plus confirmation on KMS integrations and audit log locations. we have the SOC2 and can provide an addendum for private deploy. we also support customer-managed KMS and HSM for private.
01:45 Samir: two questions: 1) will logs show token-level info in the console? 2) what's retention by default?
01:52 Maya: good Q. default retention in hosted is 30 days but can be extended, and logs in Redwood Console include request metadata but token text is redacted unless you enable full transcript logging for debugging; for Private deployments you control retention and we can turn on local audit logs.
02:10 Samir: ok that helps. also need SAML/SSO mapping for roles.
02:15 Maya: yes we support SAML/SSO and RBAC mapping, can share the SAML metadata and example role mappings.
02:22 Elena: for VPC peering, we need the ASN and IP ranges from Redwood so we can configure on our side.
02:28 Maya: I'll put that in the notes; Devon, can you add the networking details?
02:33 Devon: yep, I'll add VPC CIDR examples and the peering steps. note that for Dedicated we usually recommend a /24 peering block to avoid overlap, and we support both cross-account peering and transit gateway.
02:46 Elena: perfect. for k8s we'll need a service account and a kubeconfig for the staging namespace. can we limit to namespace-scoped access?
02:54 Devon: yes namespace scoped is fine. we'll need a short-lived service account token or a kubeconfig with the role binding.
03:02 Priya: question on model variants, are we using quantized models for cost reasons in Dedicated? we saw mention of 4-bit quantization in the docs.
03:11 Devon: yep, we recommend quantized variants for lower cost and throughput gains, but it depends on quality requirements. our Optimize suggestions will recommend a q4 or q2 based on evals. also mention, the runtime does KV cache and prefix caching which helps in chat flows.
03:27 Ravi: slight ASR hiccup earlier, I heard "Q V cache" in previous note, it's KV cache right?
03:31 Devon: yes KV cache.
03:33 Maya: for the benchmark plan, we'll run three legs: hosted baseline (Redwood API), Dedicated small pool, and on-prem staged cluster. Devon will instrument latency traces with 95/50 metrics.
03:48 Devon: right. my plan: run low concurrency ramp tests, then sustained throughput, and finally burst tests. I'll capture p95, p50, error rates, and token/sec.
03:58 Elena: any special tooling we need to open inbound rules for? the test runner will come from our CI runners in staging.
04:04 Devon: we can run from your CI; we just need the endpoint and a service account or API key. for hosted we can use API key; for Dedicated/on-prem we'll do a temporary staging key and mutual TLS if you prefer.
04:17 Samir: mutual TLS would be preferred for our security posture.
04:20 Maya: noted, we'll prepare mTLS guidance.
04:23 Ravi: on dataset access, we will provide a stripped sample dataset of 10k queries, but can't share PHI. are there options for local evals?
04:31 Devon: yes we can run eval harness locally in your environment; you can share metrics only. that's how we do private evals to preserve data privacy.
04:39 Priya: great. another thing, pricing - we need a rough pilot cost estimate for Dedicated for the two-month pilot.
04:46 Maya: I'll share a pricing sheet; rough ballpark for the small pool we'll propose in the follow-up. include notes for burst capacity.
04:53 Ravi: also, any known differences in latency between Redwood Hosted and Dedicated on same GPU type?
04:58 Devon: small differences: hosted has multi-tenant layering but we provide performance profiles; Dedicated avoids noisy neighbor and you'll usually see 5-15% lower tail latency. on-prem can vary depending on networking.
05:13 Elena: networking aside, our staging cluster is on-prem to cloud gateway so we expect some egress latency. do you have recommendations for colocating?
05:20 Devon: co-locating model serving close to data is ideal. for now we can adjust batch settings and KV cache to compensate; we'll test and then recommend quantization or smaller context windows if needed.
05:33 Maya: ok let's recap the blockers: 1) staging k8s access (Elena/Samir), 2) VPC peering details (Nexa to provide), 3) security pack from Redwood, 4) scheduling benchmark window.
05:46 Ravi: timeline wise we aim to complete benchmarks by 2027-02-18 and decide pilot terms by end of Feb.
05:52 Maya: sounds reasonable. Devon any risks we should flag?
05:56 Devon: risk: if we can't provision enough GPU for on-prem test, the numbers will be misleading. mitigation: we'll label which tests are constrained and run a scaled down simulation. also watch out for tokenization differences across model variants which can affect latency.
06:12 Priya: tokenization question - if we switch quantized model, will outputs be identical?
06:16 Devon: usually very close, sometimes micro differences. that's why we run quality evals on your prompt set.
06:23 Elena: on the SSO front, Samir will own mapping, we'll share SAML metadata by Monday.
06:28 Samir: yes, will do.
06:30 Jordan: action items I'll capture and drop into the CRM record. Maya will send the security docs and pricing.
06:36 Maya: ok I'll send the security pack and the dedicated pricing by Friday.
06:40 Ravi: one more thing - backups and data residency for audit review, we need to confirm EU data residency for any logs if we ship to EU customers.
06:49 Maya: for hosted we have region selection and residency options; for Private you control storage location. we'll include the residency note in the security pack.
06:57 Devon: quick note about tooling: we'll provide a small runbook for reproducing perf tests and a spreadsheet template to collect the results.
07:05 Priya: perfect, that will help.
07:08 Maya: ok next steps recap - we've captured them, we'll follow up with all artifacts. does anyone have anything else to add?
07:14 Ravi: nope that's it, thanks everyone.
07:16 Elena: thanks all.
07:17 Maya: great thanks, we'll talk next week same time.
07:21 End of transcript.

References mentioned: security pack link (internal): https://redwood.example.com/security/nexa-poc, dedicated pricing spreadsheet (link shared after), runbook template (will be attached in follow-up).

Notes on transcription: medium quality, a few misrecognized product words ("Redwood privatee", "Q V cache"); speaker labels mostly accurate but may have swapped Samir/Elena in a couple short exchanges.
